translations.en: Well, well! You brought it back.
Excellent, excellent.
You hand the delighted @7rAnselm@0r
@7rAnselm's@0r @3rSpellbook@0r, which you retrieved.
Yes, this is certainly it.
See, here are my scribbles in the book.
You've done your job perfectly.
Now, here's your reward. Please take it.
From @7rAnselm@0r, as your reward, you received
I may have more requests like this,
ones that must be kept secret from @7rBeatrix@0r.
I'll be counting on you then.
It seems there are plenty more jobs of this kind.
You would probably do well to go along with them.
After all, they pay well as official requests,
and you might obtain some valuable information.
Please find her soon and get it back.
And remember, not a word to @7rBeatrix@0r.
Oh? Have you decided to take the job?
There's no one else I can trust as I trust you.
Won't you please accept?
It seems simple enough, so you nod your agreement.
Then @7rAnselm@0r adds another condition.
Oh, yes, I nearly forgot something important.
Please keep this request
a secret from @7rBeatrix@0r.
If she learned that someone I'd lent an important magic textbook to
was carrying it around the ruins, @7rBeatrix@0r would cause quite a scene.
At worst, that mage might find her head
separated from her body.
Well, I'm counting on you.
Her party isn't very skilled,
so I expect she'll be on one of the upper levels.
Oh, yes. The mage's name is @7rRiz@0r.
So this is to be a secret request.
It is certainly true that @7rBeatrix@0r or @7rCarmine@0r
might do just what he described.
For now, you should carry out @7rAnselm's@0r request
and search the ruins for @7rRiz the Mage@0r.
Surely looking for people is not your kind of work.
You say as much, shake your head, and refuse.
I see... What a predicament...
I don't know another party I could ask...
This job looks simple at first glance, and it really is simple,
but trust is what matters. And you're the only adventurers
I know I can trust...
Well, it can't be helped.
I'll wait until you're willing to accept.
There's something I'd like to ask you...
May I?
It's nothing difficult.
I'd like you to find a mage who often goes
antique hunting in the ruins.
I called at her house earlier,
but she'd already left for the labyrinth.
I lent that mage a book needed to unravel
the curse on this city, and she hasn't returned it.
Her family tells me she's carrying it with her.
So I'd like you to find her
and get the book back.
Will you take the job?
You received a @3rParalysis Dagger@0r and ten @3rTeleport Scroll@0rs.
Whew! You really saved me back there.
Those creeps thought I was so cute,
they were going to sacrifice me to a demon!
Devil worship is so out of fashion these days, too.
Honestly, the nerve!
But I'm glad you're safe.
Sorry I worried you!
Anyway, thanks for saving me.
Yes! Thank you for saving @7rFiore@0r!
Here, this is to thank you for rescuing her.
As a reward, @7rTanya@0r gave you @3r30,000 G@0r.
What? You're charging a rescue fee?
The thing is, I don't have any money on me.
It's fine. @7rTanya@0r asked you to help,
so @7rTanya@0r will pay.
Oh, I can't let you do that.
Here, take these as my thanks. They're valuable!
From @7rFiore@0r, you received a @3rParalysis Dagger@0r and ten @3rTeleport Scroll@0rs.

context: Anselm receives his spellbook and explains secret retrieval from Riz, explicitly female in E1711; Fiore is rescued from would-be sacrificers.
decisions: Control tokens remain on their source rows and in their original sequence. Genuine sentence continuations retain row boundaries; other omitted subjects are restored from scene context. Unknown historical warrior gender stays neutral. Item names follow the shared glossary; established imported prose and provenance remain intact.
